entities.summary: Anita Catarina Malfatti is heralded as the first Brazilian artist to introduce European and American forms of Modernism to Brazil. Her solo exhibition in São Paulo, in 1917–1918, was controversial at the time, and her expressionist style and subject were revolutionary for the complacently old-fashioned art expectations of Brazilians who were searching for a national identity in art, but who were not prepared for the influences Malfatti would bring to the country. Malfatti's presence was also highly felt during the Week of Modern Art in 1922, where she and the Group of Five made huge revolutionary changes in the structure and response to modern art in Brazil.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Malfatti's introduction of Modernism to Brazil led to a significant shift in the country's artistic landscape, influencing generations of artists and contributing to the development of Brazilian modern art. Her work during the Week of Modern Art in 1922 helped establish a new era of artistic innovation in Brazil.
